_comment: Copy to ops/alerts.json and edit, or compose a rule in the console at /app and paste it in. That copy is gitignored: it names your addresses and your thresholds, and a threshold published is a thing an attacker knows to sit just underneath. Every rule here NOTIFIES and nothing more — ops/alerts.ts holds no key, signs nothing and builds no transaction.

telegram._comment: Optional. WARDA_TELEGRAM_CHAT in ops/alerts.env wins if set. The TOKEN is never kept here — a rule file gets pasted into chat windows.

rules.note: Agent #003 buys #001's digest daily and does not refill itself.
rules._below: Optional. Defaults to the grant's own max_per_spend: below its per-payment cap it can no longer make a payment of the size it was authorised for, whatever the counters say.
rules._needed: Optional. What the SUCCESSOR would cost — its budget plus the genesis fee. Only used to say whether the funder could pay for it.
rules._funder: Optional, and an ADDRESS, never a key. Given one, the message says whether the next grant can be paid for and whether it is in one coin. Omitted, nothing is claimed about it.

rules.note: A grant past its term refuses every spend whatever its budget says.
rules._within: Blocks. Kaspa is ten per second, so 3600 is about six minutes and 86400 is a day.

rules.note: The demo vendor's takings. When they are worth converting, say so.
rules._atOrAbove: SOMPI. Not dollars: a cron job that converted dollars would have to fetch a price, and a price fetched by a machine at 3am is a number nobody said. The console does the conversion once, in front of you, and writes down both.

quote._comment: What you meant by that figure. Shown in the message, never compared against. The rate is whatever was true when you wrote the rule; the alert does not re-check it and does not pretend to.
